title: Convention and reinvention
instructions:
Two things sit on this lens. Reinvention: cr attaches pre-existing symbols that resemble what the diff added, and you decide whether one of them already does the work. Standards: the rules attached to this unit are the project's own, and those rules, not this text, say how code here is written. A standard that is not in the corpus is not a standard yet, and belongs in a rule the project can review rather than in a comment to one author.

A resembling symbol is a question, never a verdict. The author may have read it and rejected it for a reason the diff does not show, and asking costs nothing while being wrong costs the standing you need for the next review. When a rule applies, quote its rationale, so the author learns the standard and not only the violation.
focus: Does an existing symbol already do this, or does it only look similar?
Which attached rule does this depart from, and what is its rationale?
Is this a standard the project has written down, or a preference of your own?
